milestones.title: 00 · Foundations & tooling
milestones.description: Everything components depend on: hooks for controlled state, focus traps, dismiss behaviour, portals, live-region announcements, SSR safety and the scaffolds that keep component work uniform.

milestones.title: 01 · Core primitives
milestones.description: The smallest building blocks — Button, IconButton, Link, Text, Heading, VisuallyHidden, Spinner, Badge, Kbd, Avatar. These set the API, token and testing conventions every later component copies.

milestones.title: 02 · Form controls
milestones.description: Labelled, validated, error-announcing controls that work with screen readers, keyboards, IME composition and RTL input. Includes the Field primitive that makes label/description/error wiring automatic.

milestones.title: 03 · Overlays & messaging
milestones.description: Layered UI: dialogs, drawers, popovers, tooltips, menus, toasts and a command palette. Focus restoration, scroll locking, portal stacking and Escape semantics are shared primitives, not per-component rewrites.

milestones.title: 04 · Navigation & structure
milestones.description: Tabs, accordions, disclosure, breadcrumbs, pagination, steppers, tree views and skip links. Roving tabindex and arrow-key semantics must be identical in LTR and RTL.

milestones.title: 05 · Data display
milestones.description: Tables, progress, meters, skeletons, empty states, cards and timelines — read correctly by screen readers and reflowed at 320px without horizontal scrolling.

milestones.title: 06 · RTL & Arabic internationalization
milestones.description: Bidi isolation, Arabic typography, numerals, calendars, pluralization, mirrored icons and a real device and screen-reader matrix for Arabic locales.

milestones.title: 07 · Accessibility conformance
milestones.description: WCAG 2.2 AA evidence rather than claims: keyboard-only, screen reader, forced-colors, zoom/reflow, text-spacing, reduced-motion and target-size audits, plus the ACR that records the results.

milestones.title: 08 · Documentation & Storybook
milestones.description: A docs site built from the same source as Storybook: usage guidance, keyboard tables, ARIA contracts, RTL notes, code that can be copied and run, and a published accessibility statement.

milestones.title: 09 · Quality engineering
milestones.description: The test strategy: coverage per directory, mutation testing of the tricky primitives, visual regression for LTR/RTL/dark, browser matrix, flake control, SSR and published-tarball tests.

milestones.title: 10 · Release & distribution
milestones.description: Changesets, provenance-signed publishing, exports validation, tree-shaking, size budgets, docs deployment and a support policy that states exactly what versions and browsers are covered.

milestones.title: 11 · Adoption, theming & DX
milestones.description: What it takes to adopt the library: theming and dark mode, framework guides (Next.js RSC, Vite, Remix), Figma token sync, codemods and a starter template that ships RTL by default.

issues.title: Add custom lint rules for accessibility invariants
issues.body:
## Context

jsx-a11y catches standard mistakes, but not this repository's invariants: no positive tabindex, no physical margins, no icon-only control without a name.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Rule (or script) rejects positive tabindex values in src
- [ ] Rule rejects ml-/mr-/pl-/pr-/left-/right- utilities in component sources
- [ ] Rule requires an accessible name prop on icon-only components
- [ ] Violations include the offending file and a link to the documentation that explains the rule
- [ ] Rules are tested with the RuleTester where applicable

## Definition of done

- [ ] Documented in the repository (README, docs page or ADR) where a consumer or contributor will look for it
- [ ] A changeset is added when the change is user-facing
- [ ] CI is green and the PR references this issue

issues.title: Define and enforce the supported browser baseline
issues.body:
## Context

Logical properties, :has, inert and CSS nesting all have different support floors. The library needs a stated baseline and a Browserslist that matches it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Browserslist config committed and referenced by the README
- [ ] Baseline includes Safari 16.4+, Chrome 111+, Firefox 120+ (rationale documented)
- [ ] inert and logical properties availability verified against the chosen baseline
- [ ] A CI check fails when a dependency raises the effective baseline unexpectedly
- [ ] The policy states what happens to older browsers (no polyfill, documented fallback)

## Definition of done

- [ ] CI is green and the PR references this issue

issues.title: Decide the composition strategy (asChild vs polymorphic as)
issues.body:
## Context

Button, Link and Heading all need to render as something else. Choosing between an asChild slot, a polymorphic as prop, and fixed components has consequences for typing, refs and accessibility that must be settled once.

## What is in scope

- Evaluate asChild (Radix-style), polymorphic as, and explicit components
- Consider TypeScript ergonomics, ref forwarding and the risk of losing semantics

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ADR committed under docs/adr with the decision, alternatives and consequences
- [ ] Prototype implemented for Button + Link showing the chosen approach
- [ ] Prototype proves aria attributes and refs survive the composition
- [ ] Rule documented for when composition is allowed at all (never to fake semantics)
- [ ] Decision reflected in the scaffolding template

## Definition of done

- [ ] Documented in the repository (README, docs page or ADR) where a consumer or contributor will look for it
- [ ] A changeset is added when the change is user-facing
- [ ] CI is green and the PR references this issue

issues.title: Implement useControllableState for every dual-mode control
issues.body:
## Context

Every stateful component must work both controlled and uncontrolled. Today that logic would be copy-pasted per component, which is how prop-sync bugs start.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Hook accepts value, defaultValue, onChange and a name for warnings
- [ ] Switching from uncontrolled to controlled warns in development, as React does
- [ ] Changing the controlled value prop updates the rendered state without an extra render
- [ ] Form reset restores defaultValue, verified by a test using a real <form> reset
- [ ] Covered by tests that assert the callback fires exactly once per change

## Definition of done

issues.title: Implement useDismiss for outside pointer, Escape, scroll and route changes
issues.body:
## Context

Dismissal behaviour is currently reinvented in each overlay. A shared hook makes it consistent, testable and correct for touch and keyboard users.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pointer-down outside dismisses, but a drag that starts inside and ends outside does not
- [ ] Escape dismissal is opt-in per surface and never fires for a closed surface
- [ ] Scroll and resize dismissal are configurable and off by default for modals
- [ ] Listeners are passive and removed on unmount (verified with a listener count assertion)
- [ ] Works inside shadow DOM containers, tested with a fixture

issues.title: Add useEventCallback and useLatest utilities
issues.body:
## Context

Overlay listeners must see the latest props without re-subscribing on every render. Without a stable callback pattern, event handlers resubscribe constantly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Safe when the component unmounts between event registration and invocation
- [ ] Tests assert the identity is stable across renders and the latest props are used
- [ ] Documented as internal API, not exported from the package entry point

issues.title: Build the focus-trap primitive with nested-layer support
issues.body:
## Context

Dialog, Drawer, AlertDialog, Menu and CommandPalette all need a correct trap. It is subtle: nested traps, portals, dynamic tabbable content, and focus that must never escape to the page.

## What is in scope

- Tab and Shift+Tab wrap inside the topmost layer only
- A paused trap is restored when a nested layer closes
- Focus returns to the element that was focused before the trap activated

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Built on the existing getTabbableElements utility, with tests for dynamic content added after mount
- [ ] Nested traps: only the top layer keeps focus; closing it restores the parent trap
- [ ] If the active element is removed from the DOM, focus moves to the container rather than body
- [ ] No scroll jump when focus is moved
- [ ] Playwright test proves Tab cannot reach the inert background of an open dialog

## Definition of done

- [ ] Documented in the repository (README, docs page or ADR) where a consumer or contributor will look for it
- [ ] A changeset is added when the change is user-facing
- [ ] CI is green and the PR references this issue

issues.title: Define the icon foundation and mirroring registry
issues.body:
## Context

Icons are 24 aria-hidden SVGs with a registry that states whether each one mirrors in RTL. Without that registry, directional icons silently point the wrong way in Arabic.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Base Icon component defaults to aria-hidden and focusable="false"
- [ ] Registry marks each icon as mirror / never-mirror, with a test that fails when a new icon is unclassified
- [ ] Icons inherit currentColor and scale with the control size
- [ ] Chevrons, arrows and back/forward mirror; checkmarks, close glyphs and play controls do not
- [ ] Bundle impact measured: icons are individually importable, not a single barrel

## Definition of done

- [ ] Documented in the repository (README, docs page or ADR) where a consumer or contributor will look for it

issues.title: Add LiveRegionProvider and useAnnounce for screen reader announcements
issues.body:
## Context

Toasts, form errors and async result counts all need announcements. A single provider prevents duplicate regions and the classic "region inserted with content is never announced" bug.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Polite and assertive regions are mounted on first render, before any message is queued
- [ ] Messages are cleared and re-set so identical consecutive messages are announced
- [ ] Queueing respects a minimum interval to avoid flooding
- [ ] Hook returns a stable announce function that is safe to call after unmount
- [ ] Tests assert the region content changes and that no duplicate live regions exist

issues.title: Build the anchored positioning primitive for popups
issues.body:
## Context

Popover, Tooltip, Menu, Combobox and DatePicker all need collision-aware positioning that understands writing direction. Doing it once is the difference between five bugs and one.

## What is in scope

- Logical placements (start, end, top, bottom) resolved against dir
- Flip and shift on collision with the viewport, with a configurable padding
- Arrow element positioning that stays within the surface radius

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Placement start resolves to the right side in RTL without prop changes
- [ ] Collision flips are tested at all four viewport edges, in both directions
- [ ] Position updates on scroll and resize are throttled to animation frames
- [ ] Position is correct inside a transformed container (documented limitation if unsupported)
- [ ] No layout thrash: single-pass measurement with ResizeObserver
- [ ] Decide build vs. adopt (floating-ui) in an ADR and record the trade-off

## Definition of done

- [ ] Documented in the repository (README, docs page or ADR) where a consumer or contributor will look for it
- [ ] A changeset is added when the change is user-facing

issues.title: Add a portal layer stack with deterministic z-index ordering
issues.body:
## Context

Dialog opens a Popover that opens a Menu: without a stack, the newest layer can render below an older one, and closing order breaks.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A LayerProvider renders portals into a container appended to document.body once per app
- [ ] Each opened layer receives an incrementing index mapped to a CSS variable, not a hard-coded z-index
- [ ] Closing a middle layer does not reorder the remaining layers
- [ ] SSR renders children without touching document, and hydration does not duplicate containers
- [ ] Toasts always sit above dialogs through an explicit layer type, not a magic number

## Definition of done

- [ ] Documented in the repository (README, docs page or ADR) where a consumer or contributor will look for it
- [ ] A changeset is added when the change is user-facing
- [ ] CI is green and the PR references this issue

issues.title: Implement scroll locking without layout shift
issues.body:

issues.title: Avatar — core implementation and public API
issues.body:
## Context

A person or entity image with initials fallback. Either the image carries a name or the whole avatar is decorative — never both, and never an alt text that duplicates the adjacent label.

## Scope

- Props: src, name (required for alt and fallback), size, decorative, status indicator
- Fallback initials derived from the name using Intl.Segmenter so Arabic names work
- Image error state falls back without layout shift
- Status dot is aria-hidden and paired with visible text elsewhere

## Accessibility contract

- Decorative mode sets alt="" and aria-hidden on the wrapper
- Named mode uses the person name as alt, not "avatar" or a file name
- No role="img" wrapper when the inner image already provides the name

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The public API matches the scope above; every prop is typed and documented
- [ ] `ref` forwards to the underlying DOM node and `className` is merged rather than replaced
- [ ] Every color, spacing, radius and duration comes from an `--aui-*` token — no literal values in the source
- [ ] Controlled and uncontrolled usage both work, including form reset and a changing `defaultValue`
- [ ] Invalid usage produces a development-only warning naming the offending prop (for example a missing accessible name)
- [ ] SSR-safe: renders with `renderToString` and hydrates without a mismatch warning
- [ ] Documentation page and stories are added in the follow-up issues, not stubbed with TODOs

## Definition of done

- [ ] Exported from `src/index.ts` with TSDoc on the public props
- [ ] `npm run verify` passes locally and in CI
- [ ] A changeset is added (`minor` for a new component, `patch` for a fix) so the changelog stays honest.
- [ ] Issue closed by a PR that references it (`Closes #…`)

## References

- WCAG 2.2: https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/

issues.title: Avatar — keyboard interaction and focus management
issues.body:
## Context

Pointer support is not a keyboard contract. This issue makes every path through `Avatar` reachable, operable and visible without a mouse, and proves it with tests.

## Keyboard contract

Not interactive; avatar links wrap the component in a Link with a proper name

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The documented key map is implemented exactly as written above
- [ ] Focus is always visible: the token-based ring is never clipped and never removed by a reset
- [ ] Tab order follows DOM order — no positive `tabindex` values anywhere in the component
- [ ] Disabled states remain discoverable where WCAG allows it (`aria-disabled` kept focusable) and are documented when removed from the tab order
- [ ] Focus is not lost when content is conditionally rendered or removed
- [ ] Directional keys are tested in both LTR and RTL where the pattern requires it
- [ ] A Playwright spec asserts each key path and the element that ends up focused

## Definition of done

- [ ] Exported from `src/index.ts` with TSDoc on the public props
- [ ] `npm run verify` passes locally and in CI
- [ ] A changeset is added (`minor` for a new component, `patch` for a fix) so the changelog stays honest.
- [ ] Issue closed by a PR that references it (`Closes #…`)

issues.title: Avatar — ARIA semantics and screen reader contract
issues.body:
## Context

`Avatar` claims to implement the **Decorative image with fallback** pattern. This issue makes the claim testable: correct roles, states and names, verified with automation and a manual screen reader pass.

## Semantics

- Decorative mode sets alt="" and aria-hidden on the wrapper
- Named mode uses the person name as alt, not "avatar" or a file name
- No role="img" wrapper when the inner image already provides the name

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Roles, states and properties are exactly those listed above — no extra `role` or `aria-*` attributes "for safety"
- [ ] The accessible name is correct for every state, including loading and error states
- [ ] axe-core reports zero WCAG A/AA violations in LTR, RTL and dark mode
- [ ] Manual screen reader walkthrough completed on VoiceOver + Safari and NVDA + Firefox, with the script and observations pasted in a comment
- [ ] Live-region announcements (where applicable) are neither duplicated nor cut off mid-sentence
- [ ] No dangling `aria-describedby` / `aria-controls` references after a state change or unmount

## Definition of done

- [ ] Exported from `src/index.ts` with TSDoc on the public props
- [ ] `npm run verify` passes locally and in CI
- [ ] A changeset is added (`minor` for a new component, `patch` for a fix) so the changelog stays honest.
- [ ] Issue closed by a PR that references it (`Closes #…`)

## References

- WCAG 2.2: https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/
- Accessibility Object Model notes: https://wicg.github.io/aom/

issues.title: Avatar — RTL, bidi and Arabic content handling
issues.body:
## Context

A component that only flips its layout is not RTL-ready. This issue covers geometry, bidi text, numerals, Arabic typography and the tests that keep them true for `Avatar`.

## RTL requirements

- Initials for Arabic names use the first letter of the first and last word with correct bidi ordering
- Fallback text is centered logically, not with a left offset
- Status indicator position mirrors with the writing direction

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All spacing and positioning uses logical properties; `grep -E "\b(ml|mr|pl|pr|left|right)-"` returns no hits in the component source
- [ ] Logical utilities are used for alignment (`text-start` / `text-end`) and icons mirror only when directional
- [ ] An Arabic story (`lang="ar"`, `dir="rtl"`) renders without clipped diacritics, broken words or overlapping glyphs
- [ ] Embedded Latin identifiers, numbers and URLs are bidi-isolated (`bdi` or `dir="ltr"` spans)
- [ ] Numerals follow an explicit decision per locale rather than the font default
- [ ] Playwright story test runs in the `chromium-rtl-ar` project and the screenshot is added to the visual baseline

## Definition of done

- [ ] Exported from `src/index.ts` with TSDoc on the public props
- [ ] `npm run verify` passes locally and in CI
- [ ] A changeset is added (`minor` for a new component, `patch` for a fix) so the changelog stays honest.
- [ ] Issue closed by a PR that references it (`Closes #…`)

## References

- WCAG 2.2: https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/
- Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm: https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/
- CSS Logical Properties: https://www.w3.org/TR/css-logical-1/

issues.title: Badge — core implementation and public API
issues.body:
## Context

A compact status token. Color is never the only signal: every tone carries text, and decorative dots are hidden from assistive technology.

## Scope

- Props: tone (neutral, accent, success, warning, danger), size, dot
- Dot is aria-hidden; the text always states the status
- Optional removable affordance is out of scope (belongs to Chip, tracked separately)
- Counts use Intl.NumberFormat with the active locale

- No role by default; status semantics come from surrounding text
- aria-label is only used when the visible text is an abbreviation
- Dot and icons are aria-hidden

- [ ] The public API matches the scope above; every prop is typed and documented

issues.title: Button — core implementation and public API
issues.body:
## Context

The reference implementation for every convention in the library: token-only styling, 44px minimum target, a loading state announced with aria-busy, and no icon-only usage without a name. Variants: primary, secondary, ghost, danger. Sizes: sm, md, lg.

## Scope

- Props: variant, size, isLoading, loadingLabel, leadingIcon, trailingIcon, fullWidth, type (defaults to button)

- Pressed state is out of scope here and belongs to ToggleButton

issues.body:
## Context

## Scope

- Props: keys (array of key tokens, including modifiers), separator, size
- Maps logical keys (Next, Previous, Start, End) to ArrowRight/ArrowLeft per direction
- Renders a single kbd element per key with visually hidden separators for screen readers
- No use of the literal arrow characters in accessible names without a spelled-out alternative

## Accessibility contract

- Native kbd semantics; no role
- Visually hidden text expands abbreviations such as Ctrl to Control
- Sequences are read in the correct order by screen readers

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The public API matches the scope above; every prop is typed and documented

issues.title: Combobox — RTL, bidi and Arabic content handling
issues.body:
## Context

A component that only flips its layout is not RTL-ready. This issue covers geometry, bidi text, numerals, Arabic typography and the tests that keep them true for `Combobox`.

## RTL requirements

- Arrow keys stay physical; the visual list order follows the writing direction
- The popup is anchored with logical inset values, not left/right offsets
- Arabic filtering is diacritic-insensitive when the caller uses the provided matcher helper

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All spacing and positioning uses logical properties; `grep -E "\b(ml|mr|pl|pr|left|right)-"` returns no hits in the component source

- [ ] An Arabic story (`lang="ar"`, `dir="rtl"`) renders without clipped diacritics, broken words or overlapping glyphs
- [ ] Embedded Latin identifiers, numbers and URLs are bidi-isolated (`bdi` or `dir="ltr"` spans)

issues.title: Field — core implementation and public API
issues.body:
## Context

The primitive that makes labelling automatic: it generates ids, wires label, description and error text with aria-describedby, and marks invalid state with aria-invalid. Every form control consumes it.

## Scope

- Props: label, description, error, required, optionalLabel, children as render function receiving ids and aria props
- Generates stable ids with useId; no duplicate ids when multiple instances render
- Error text is announced politely and is never the only indicator of failure (icon + text + aria-invalid)
- Supports fieldset/legend mode for checkbox and radio groups through Fieldset

## Accessibility contract

- label[for] association, or aria-labelledby when the label contains rich content
- aria-describedby combines description and error ids in a stable order
- aria-invalid="true" only when an error is present and after the field has been touched
- Required is conveyed with the required attribute, not an asterisk alone

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The public API matches the scope above; every prop is typed and documented
- [ ] `ref` forwards to the underlying DOM node and `className` is merged rather than replaced
- [ ] Every color, spacing, radius and duration comes from an `--aui-*` token — no literal values in the source
- [ ] Controlled and uncontrolled usage both work, including form reset and a changing `defaultValue`
- [ ] Invalid usage produces a development-only warning naming the offending prop (for example a missing accessible name)
- [ ] SSR-safe: renders with `renderToString` and hydrates without a mismatch warning
- [ ] Documentation page and stories are added in the follow-up issues, not stubbed with TODOs

issues.title: NumberField — core implementation and public API
issues.body:
## Context

Numeric input with stepper buttons, locale-aware formatting and an explicit decision about Arabic-Indic digits in both display and submitted value.

This component composes `input`, so those issues must land first.

## Scope

- Props: value, onValueChange, min, max, step, formatOptions, locale, allowWheel
- Displayed value can be localized while the submitted value stays a JavaScript number
- Stepper buttons are labelled, repeat on long press, and are hidden from the tab order when reaching a bound
- Rejects non-numeric input without destroying the user text on every keystroke

## Accessibility contract

- role="spinbutton" with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuetext when formatted
- Stepper buttons have accessible names, not just plus/minus glyphs
- Invalid input is announced with aria-invalid and a described error

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The public API matches the scope above; every prop is typed and documented
- [ ] `ref` forwards to the underlying DOM node and `className` is merged rather than replaced
- [ ] Every color, spacing, radius and duration comes from an `--aui-*` token — no literal values in the source
- [ ] Controlled and uncontrolled usage both work, including form reset and a changing `defaultValue`
- [ ] Invalid usage produces a development-only warning naming the offending prop (for example a missing accessible name)
- [ ] SSR-safe: renders with `renderToString` and hydrates without a mismatch warning
- [ ] Documentation page and stories are added in the follow-up issues, not stubbed with TODOs

- [ ] Exported from `src/index.ts` with TSDoc on the public props

`ContextMenu` claims to implement the **Context menu** pattern. This issue makes the claim testable: correct roles, states and names, verified with automation and a manual screen reader pass.

## Semantics

- Same menu roles as Menu; the invoking element is not given a fake role
- The menu is labelled by the region it applies to
- Screen reader users can discover the shortcut through visible hint text

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Roles, states and properties are exactly those listed above — no extra `role` or `aria-*` attributes "for safety"
- [ ] The accessible name is correct for every state, including loading and error states
- [ ] axe-core reports zero WCAG A/AA violations in LTR, RTL and dark mode
- [ ] Manual screen reader walkthrough completed on VoiceOver + Safari and NVDA + Firefox, with the script and observations pasted in a comment
- [ ] Live-region announcements (where applicable) are neither duplicated nor cut off mid-sentence
- [ ] No dangling `aria-describedby` / `aria-controls` references after a state change or unmount

## Definition of done

- [ ] Exported from `src/index.ts` with TSDoc on the public props
- [ ] `npm run verify` passes locally and in CI

issues.title: ContextMenu — RTL, bidi and Arabic content handling
issues.body:
## Context

A component that only flips its layout is not RTL-ready. This issue covers geometry, bidi text, numerals, Arabic typography and the tests that keep them true for `ContextMenu`.

## RTL requirements

- Pointer coordinates are physical, submenu direction keys are logical
- The menu clamps to the inline-end edge in both directions
- Shortcut hints align to the inline-end edge

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All spacing and positioning uses logical properties; `grep -E "\b(ml|mr|pl|pr|left|right)-"` returns no hits in the component source
- [ ] Logical utilities are used for alignment (`text-start` / `text-end`) and icons mirror only when directional
- [ ] An Arabic story (`lang="ar"`, `dir="rtl"`) renders without clipped diacritics, broken words or overlapping glyphs
- [ ] Embedded Latin identifiers, numbers and URLs are bidi-isolated (`bdi` or `dir="ltr"` spans)

issues.title: DatePicker — core implementation and public API
issues.body:
## Context

A text input for typing a date plus a calendar dialog for choosing one. It supports the Hijri (Umm al-Qura) calendar, not just Gregorian, and never assumes Western digits or Sunday-first weeks.

This component composes `dialog`, `popover`, `field`, so those issues must land first.

## Scope

- Props: value, onValueChange, locale, calendar (gregory, islamic-umalqura), min, max, disabledDates
- Typed input is parsed with the active locale and calendar; invalid text keeps user input and explains the format
- Calendar grid uses a real table with row/column headers, roving tabindex and aria-selected
- Today is identified textually, not by color; weekends are not assumed to be Saturday/Sunday

## Accessibility contract

- Input has an accessible name and format hint; the dialog is labelled by the month and year
- Grid cells expose the full date in the accessible name, not just the day number
- Selected and disabled dates are conveyed with aria-selected and aria-disabled
- Month/year changes are announced politely

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The public API matches the scope above; every prop is typed and documented
- [ ] `ref` forwards to the underlying DOM node and `className` is merged rather than replaced
- [ ] Every color, spacing, radius and duration comes from an `--aui-*` token — no literal values in the source
- [ ] Controlled and uncontrolled usage both work, including form reset and a changing `defaultValue`
- [ ] Invalid usage produces a development-only warning naming the offending prop (for example a missing accessible name)
- [ ] SSR-safe: renders with `renderToString` and hydrates without a mismatch warning
- [ ] Documentation page and stories are added in the follow-up issues, not stubbed with TODOs

## Definition of done

- [ ] Exported from `src/index.ts` with TSDoc on the public props
- [ ] `npm run verify` passes locally and in CI
- [ ] A changeset is added (`minor` for a new component, `patch` for a fix) so the changelog stays honest.
- [ ] Issue closed by a PR that references it (`Closes #…`)

## References

- WCAG 2.2: https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/

issues.title: Dialog — core implementation and public API
issues.body:
## Context

The modal primitive every other overlay reuses: focus trap, background inerting, scroll lock, labelled and described content, focus restoration, and nested-dialog stacking that does not corrupt the tab order.

This component composes `button`, `visually-hidden`, so those issues must land first.

## Scope

- Props: open, onOpenChange, title, description, size, initialFocusRef, closeOnEscape, closeOnInteractOutside, showCloseButton
- Focus is trapped through the shared useFocusTrap primitive; the background is inert, not merely covered
- Opening focuses the initial target, falling back to the dialog container; closing restores the previously focused element
- Portals render into a layer stack so nested dialogs and toasts keep correct z-order

## Accessibility contract

- role="dialog" with aria-modal="true", aria-labelledby pointing at the title and aria-describedby at the description
- A dialog without an accessible name is a test failure, not a warning
- Background content receives inert/aria-hidden exactly once, restored on close
- The close button has a localized accessible name

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The public API matches the scope above; every prop is typed and documented
- [ ] `ref` forwards to the underlying DOM node and `className` is merged rather than replaced
- [ ] Every color, spacing, radius and duration comes from an `--aui-*` token — no literal values in the source
- [ ] Controlled and uncontrolled usage both work, including form reset and a changing `defaultValue`
- [ ] Invalid usage produces a development-only warning naming the offending prop (for example a missing accessible name)
- [ ] SSR-safe: renders with `renderToString` and hydrates without a mismatch warning
- [ ] Documentation page and stories are added in the follow-up issues, not stubbed with TODOs

issues.title: HoverCard — core implementation and public API
issues.body:
## Context

Rich preview on hover or focus for user mentions and link previews. It must never contain the only path to essential information, and it works on touch through an explicit trigger.

This component composes `popover`, so those issues must land first.

## Scope

- Props: content, children, openDelay, closeDelay, placement
- Opens on hover and focus; touch users get a tap trigger that is a real button
- Dismissible with Escape, and the card stays open while hovered
- No focus trap; content is read-only

## Accessibility contract

- Trigger is described by the card content, not labelled by it
- Content is plain text or links with names; no nested dialogs
- Closing never removes focus from the trigger

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The public API matches the scope above; every prop is typed and documented
- [ ] `ref` forwards to the underlying DOM node and `className` is merged rather than replaced
- [ ] Every color, spacing, radius and duration comes from an `--aui-*` token — no literal values in the source
- [ ] Controlled and uncontrolled usage both work, including form reset and a changing `defaultValue`
- [ ] Invalid usage produces a development-only warning naming the offending prop (for example a missing accessible name)
- [ ] SSR-safe: renders with `renderToString` and hydrates without a mismatch warning
- [ ] Documentation page and stories are added in the follow-up issues, not stubbed with TODOs

## Definition of done

- [ ] Exported from `src/index.ts` with TSDoc on the public props
- [ ] `npm run verify` passes locally and in CI
- [ ] A changeset is added (`minor` for a new component, `patch` for a fix) so the changelog stays honest.
- [ ] Issue closed by a PR that references it (`Closes #…`)

## References

issues.body:
## Context

`Menu` needs a test suite that fails when its accessibility contract regresses — not a coverage number that goes up when a trivial assertion is added.

## Required coverage

- Rendering: every variant, size and state, in LTR and RTL
- Interaction: the full keyboard contract, pointer paths and focus restoration
- Forms: controlled/uncontrolled transitions, reset, disabled and invalid states
- Async: loading, empty, error and success states with fake timers, no arbitrary sleeps
- Accessibility: axe assertion in jsdom plus the Playwright browser project

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unit tests use `render` from `src/test-utils/render.tsx` so both directions are exercised
- [ ] `expectNoA11yViolations` runs in LTR and RTL and fails the build on violations
- [ ] Playwright spec covers the keyboard map and the focus target after each key
- [ ] Visual baseline screenshots exist for LTR, RTL and dark mode
- [ ] No `waitForTimeout` in committed tests; fake timers or `findBy*` queries instead
- [ ] The suite fails when the ARIA contract is deliberately broken (verified once in the PR description)

- Dismissal never strands focus in a removed element

- [ ] `ref` forwards to the underlying DOM node and `className` is merged rather than replaced

## Context

This component composes `button`, so those issues must land first.

- The toast itself does not receive focus on appearance
- Dismissal does not move focus unexpectedly

issues.title: Toast — ARIA semantics and screen reader contract
issues.body:
## Context

`Toast` claims to implement the **Status message and alert** pattern. This issue makes the claim testable: correct roles, states and names, verified with automation and a manual screen reader pass.

## Semantics

- Container is a live region that exists before the first toast (otherwise nothing is announced)
- role="status" for info/success, role="alert" only for errors
- The toast itself does not receive focus on appearance
- Dismissal does not move focus unexpectedly

issues.body:
## Context

issues.title: Tooltip — core implementation and public API
issues.body:
## Context

Supplemental text on hover and focus. It uses aria-describedby, dismisses with Escape, stays open while the pointer is over it (WCAG 1.4.13), and never holds interactive content.

This component composes `popover`, `visually-hidden`, so those issues must land first.

## Scope

- Props: content, children, placement, delayMs, closeDelayMs, disabled
- Opens on hover and on focus, closes on Escape, blur, pointer leave and scroll
- Hoverable: the tooltip itself keeps the pointer-open state so the user can read it
- Content is text only; interactive content is rejected by types and documented

## Accessibility contract

- Trigger receives aria-describedby pointing at the tooltip id
- role="tooltip" on the surface; no aria-expanded because this is not a disclosure
- The tooltip never becomes the only accessible name of a control

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The public API matches the scope above; every prop is typed and documented
- [ ] `ref` forwards to the underlying DOM node and `className` is merged rather than replaced
- [ ] Every color, spacing, radius and duration comes from an `--aui-*` token — no literal values in the source
- [ ] Controlled and uncontrolled usage both work, including form reset and a changing `defaultValue`
- [ ] Invalid usage produces a development-only warning naming the offending prop (for example a missing accessible name)
- [ ] SSR-safe: renders with `renderToString` and hydrates without a mismatch warning
- [ ] Documentation page and stories are added in the follow-up issues, not stubbed with TODOs

## Context

- aria-disabled is used instead of disabled so headers stay discoverable
- Panels are not aria-hidden while animating open

issues.body:
## Context

Tabbed panels with roving tabindex, manual and automatic activation, vertical orientation, lazy mounting, and arrow keys that follow the visual order in both writing directions.

This component composes `button`, so those issues must land first.

## Scope

- Props: value, onValueChange, activationMode (manual, automatic), orientation, loop, lazy, unmountOnHide
- Roving tabindex: one tab in the tab order, arrow keys move, Home/End jump to the edges

- Inactive panels are hidden from assistive technology, not merely visually collapsed
- Each tab has a stable accessible name; icon-only tabs are rejected unless labelled

issues.title: Publish to npm with provenance and a protected release workflow
